newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to move 80,000 families in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to move 80,000 families in 1997/98.

text.p: Indonesia plans to speed up its resettlement programme which moves people from the overcrowded island of Java to the less populated areas of the archipelago, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Thursday.
Transmigration Minister Siswono Yudohusodo was quoted as saying Jakarta plans to move 80,000 families in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), up from a projected 76,322 families this year.
Siswono said over 50,000 of these families would be resettled in eastern Indonesia. There was no precise figure for the number of people involved in the programme.
Indonesia, the world's fourth most populous country, consists of more than 13,000 islands but the majority of the near 200 million population live on the main island of Java.
Transmigration, the official term for the resettlement programme, offers Javanese free land and housing on other islands that are sparsely populated but often remote.
The scheme has been criticised because land in resettlement areas is not suitable for many types of agriculture and infrastructure like schools and hospitals is often missing.
The report said Siswono said more than 29,000 children in transmigration sites lack a proper education because of a shortage of junior high schools.
Siswono was quoted as saying the government hoped to attract private sector investment in transmigration areas to make them more attractive for migrants.
